correctness.rationale: For every positive scale the scalar fixed point has a unique root because both moments and the aggregate cost difference are nondecreasing with the threshold; the explicit scalar term is strictly increasing. Logistic random-threshold representation yields centered variance π²/3 and exponential endpoint tails. Implicit expansion has denominator D=1+∂MΔ+θ∂EΔ>0 and yields M and E coefficients through order σ² with O(σ⁴) remainders. Exact logistic antiderivatives give the sharp L¹ coefficient 2 log 2. The h1=2ME witness has A=5/4, B=1 and D=7/4. Standalone standard-library verification produced 174 assertions. The proof, not enumeration, covers all smooth monotone costs meeting the assumptions.

value.rationale: The motivating continuum game explicitly distinguishes customer mass from energy-demand-weighted market share and requests quantitative zero-noise limits. A non-potential smooth monotone model can display the genuinely opposite signs of their first nonzero perturbations. The general A,B,D formula quantifies feedback across all eligible monotone two-moment costs; the sharp universal L¹ coefficient identifies a different perturbation scale. Thus the theorem determines structural and policy-relevant behavior, not only a routine logistic integral.
